traits: Cap 7 to 20 cm, cream, buff to cinnamon-brown: keel-shaped when young, then domed, then spreading with a boss, finally funnel-shaped; smooth margin
Fine, deeply decurrent gills, cream to buff
Solid, fibrous stem, 10 to 20 cm, very swollen when young, the colour of the cap; no ring
White flesh, firm when young · strong, sweet smell of bitter almond or hay
On the ground in broadleaf woods, edges and clearings, often in troops or rings, from late summer until the first frosts
safetyNote: Edible of middling value, only when young: the fibrous stem becomes tough and is thrown away. It is on the German mycological society list (« Mönchskopf ») and on the Swiss controllers’ list (« tête de moine »). ANSES records livid entolomas picked instead of trooping funnels (2022): the entoloma has notched gills that turn pink, a floury smell and pink spores. The miller, also edible, has pink spores.
